_comment: The narration record for the film. Revision 3 script (Talia, 2026-09-17).
scripts/synth.py reads this and writes assets/<id>.wav plus the timing
files in data/. One entry per section:
n        section number (render.py --scene N once a scene module exists)
id       file stem: assets/<id>.wav, data/words-<id>.json, cues, visemes
card     the title card or cut the script calls for at the top of the section
slot     the section's authored length in seconds. OMIT it while the scene
is unbuilt: Ava's own pace then sets the length and pacing.md
reports what each section needs. Set it once the scene exists.
nora     true when Nora is on camera, so a viseme track is written
chunks   each chunk is synthesised on its own. `at` places it at a time
inside the section; without `at` it follows the previous chunk
after `pause` seconds (default 0.45). Use `at` only once a scene
has beats to hit; until then let the read breathe naturally.
phrases  caption-sized pieces; word timings are aligned to these and
slots were frozen from Ava's natural read on 2026-09-17 so scene durations and audio stay locked together; change a slot and the scene's `dur` together

phrases: Hi, I'm Nora.
You might know me as your friendly help desk assistant.
And if we haven't met yet, it's nice to meet you!
Talia and I have been working on building a great platform that will make a real difference across Northpointe.
The platform is an Enterprise Support Portal.
The idea is One Northpointe Support Experience.
A better way for teams across the company to manage requests, communicate with the people they support, and ultimately provide a better experience for our customers.
Right now, we're trialing an application called BoldDesk, and we've been looking at what it could make possible for Northpointe.
A handful of teams have already started testing it.
And here's a thought: wouldn't it be amazing if every team was on it?
One universally great experience. Literally a one-stop shop for support, for all of Northpointe.
So, why BoldDesk?
One of the things that stood out to us is how simple it is.
A lot of ticketing systems are designed primarily with technical teams in mind.
BoldDesk is much more approachable.
It's easy for the person submitting a request, and it's easy for the person working it.
The best system in the world doesn't help us if people don't want to use it.

scenes.title: The shared mailbox
scenes.card: CUT TO: Shared mailbox / email animation

phrases: As we've talked with teams across Northpointe, we've seen a common challenge.
Requests are often living in shared Outlook mailboxes.
People are searching through email threads. Forwarding messages. CC'ing multiple people.
Trying to figure out who owns something.
Looking back through a long chain to figure out what the actual question was.
And when someone is out of the office, it can become even harder to know where something stands or what has already been done.
The result can be extra back-and-forth, longer wait times, and a lot of work happening behind the scenes just to keep track of the work itself.

scenes.title: Better experience for everyone
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: Better experience for everyone

phrases: And this isn't just an internal efficiency issue.
Every one of us supports a customer in some way.
That might be an external business partner.
It might be a borrower.
It might be a retail banking customer.
Or it might be another Northpointe employee.
And that last one matters more than we sometimes realize.
Because when we help our internal teams get what they need faster, we're helping them serve their customers faster.
Imagine someone in Sales is working with a borrower and suddenly can't access a system they need.
If that request turns into multiple emails back and forth just to figure out which application they need help with, that's time.
And while they're waiting, their customer is waiting too.
A better support experience internally can have a very real impact externally.

scenes.title: Nothing changes for the person emailing you
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: Nothing changes for the person emailing you

phrases: One thing I really like about BoldDesk is that we can improve what happens behind the scenes without making things harder for the person asking for help.
Teams can continue using their existing support email addresses.
The email becomes a ticket behind the scenes, where it can be tracked, assigned, documented, and measured.
So for the customer, the experience can stay simple.
For the team, the process becomes much more organized.
And that creates an opportunity for better and faster communication without asking the person on the other end to learn an entirely new way of working.

scenes.title: One place for everything
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: One place for everything

phrases: There is also a portal.
The portal gives Northpointe employees one place to open new requests and see the requests they already have open with teams using BoldDesk.
They can see where something stands without having to send another email asking for an update.
And the portal is mobile friendly and doesn't require a VPN, which is especially useful for people who aren't sitting at a desk all day.

For example, someone in Sales could bookmark the portal on their phone, log in with the same account they already use for Outlook and Teams, and submit a request while they're between meetings or out working with customers.
That may add 30 seconds to a minute up front to give us the information we need.
But that small amount of effort can save much more time later by reducing the back-and-forth needed to get the request worked.

scenes.title: Knowledge that works for everyone
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: Knowledge that works for everyone

phrases: The portal can also give us something else that's really valuable: a shared knowledge base.
Every team can contribute articles, helpful tips, common answers, and self-service information based on what they know.
So instead of answering the same question over and over, a team can answer it once and make that knowledge available to everyone.
What one team knows can become something the whole company can use.
And then there's visibility for the people leading these teams.
Managers can have dashboards that show what's happening across their teams at a glance.
How many requests are open?
How many are waiting on the customer?
How many have been closed?
How much work does each person have?
Are requests being answered within the expected time?
And are they being resolved within the expected time?
That visibility gives managers something we don't always have today: a clear picture of the work while it's happening.
It can help identify bottlenecks, workload issues, and opportunities to move resources where they're needed.
And it gives leadership the ability to establish measurable service expectations.
Maybe that's a common standard across Northpointe.
Maybe each team has its own SLA based on the type of work they do.
BoldDesk can support either approach.
The important part is having the ability to actually see the results.

scenes.title: Better communication. Better accountability. Better customer experience.
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: Better communication. Better accountability. Better customer experience.

phrases: That visibility also creates accountability.
When requests are tracked and SLAs are visible, it's easier to make sure customers aren't left wondering what happened to their request.
And when someone is out of the office, the rest of the team can see the ticket history and notes and pick up where things left off.
The goal isn't to make people work harder.
It's to make it easier for people to do the work they're already trying to do.
And BoldDesk doesn't have to stand alone.
It can connect with other platforms and automate repetitive work.
For example, during the trial we've tested an integration with ClickUp.
A ticket can be pushed into ClickUp as a project task with the information carried over automatically.
The ClickUp number and link can then come back into the BoldDesk ticket, keeping the two systems connected.
That's one example, but the bigger opportunity is being able to connect the tools teams already use instead of making people duplicate their work between systems.
There are also opportunities for automated responses, routing, assignment, document handling, and other repetitive tasks.
And every time we automate something repetitive, we're giving people back time to work on the things that actually need a person.

scenes.title: And down the road…
scenes.card: TITLE CARD: And down the road…

phrases: There's even room to think about what's next.

BoldDesk has an AI connector that could potentially allow things like summarizing a long ticket conversation so a manager or team member could quickly understand what's happening without reading through dozens of replies.
That's a future possibility, and something we'd want to evaluate carefully from a security and data-governance perspective.
But that's part of what makes this interesting.
We're not just looking at what the platform can do today.
We're looking at what it could grow into.

scenes.title: Why it matters
scenes.card: CUT TO: Customer / sales / employee animation

phrases: And I'll come back to the reason I think that matters.
This isn't really about moving emails from one place to another.
It's about making it easier for people to get help.
And ultimately, it's about helping the people who serve our customers do their jobs more effectively.

Because whether you're working directly with a borrower, supporting a business partner, working with a retail customer, or helping another Northpointe employee behind the scenes, we all play a part in the customer experience.
We're still exploring what this could look like across Northpointe, but the possibilities are pretty exciting.
Better tracking.
Better communication.
More visibility.
More automation.
And a better experience for the people asking for help, which can mean a better experience for the customers we're all here to serve.
I'm Nora.
Thanks for listening.
And I'll see you at the help desk!
